Subject: Hosted->Dedicated timing and rollback questions

Hi Markus,

We kicked off an internal run of our peak chat workload and want to align on the migration timeline and safety nets. Current quick stats from our end: average concurrent sessions ~420, peak streaming QPS ~240 (burst to 380 for short spikes), typical prompt length 280 tokens, p99 latency target <= 350ms.

Two asks up front:
- Can Redwood validate sizing based on our attached multiplex profile? (attaching: peregrine_multiplex_load.pdf)
- What is the documented switchback / rollback window if we hit latency/regression post-swap?

We'd like a dry-run the week of Sep 27 and target a production swap the week of Oct 11 if all green. Procurement also wants a clear acceptance checklist.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Head of Infrastructure, Peregrine Labs

Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated timing and rollback questions

Adding sizing details from our preliminary analysis of the multiplex profile. Notes below are the starting point for the validation runs.

Summary (initial rightsize estimate):
- Model family: redwood-open-12B (float16 runtime; quantization plan optional)
- Baseline: 8 x A100-80GB GPUs for steady-state (~240 QPS streaming), configured with 2 replicas and continuous batching (batch max 64)
- Burst headroom: +4 GPUs to tolerate spikes to 380 QPS for 15-60s bursts (warm pool via autoscale fast-failover)
- KV/Prefix cache: reserve 180GB distributed (expect ~30% cache hit for common prompts)
- Expected p95/p99 with this config: 180ms/320ms (on our test stack)

Validation job spec (short):
- Traffic mirror: replay 1.25x production for 45 minutes, run three passes (peak, steady, long-tail)
- Stress tests: 2x sustained for 10 minutes to validate thermal throttling and model sharding behaviors
- Telemetry: p50/p95/p99 latencies, token/sec per GPU, GPU utilization, OOM/Model errors, KV hit ratio

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: publish validation spec (today EOD) and seed perf test cluster.
- Karthik: runbook for stress and rollback automation (by Sep 22).
- Soojin: confirm autoscale policy knobs we will enable for the swap.

I will attach the validation metric dashboard after the first mirrored run.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Couple of practical verification items to call out for the stress run:

Pass/fail thresholds (examples):
- Latency: p99 <= 350ms during normal profile; any sustained p99 > 450ms for >5 minutes -> FAIL
- Error-rate: 5xxs > 0.5% of requests in any 10-minute window -> FAIL
- Token cost delta: if estimated per-token cost increases >15% (unexpected regression) -> alert (manual review)

Switchback automation notes:
- We will maintain a hot path to the hosted model and pre-populate circuit-breaker rules in the API gateway.
- Switchback steps: 1) stop routing new traffic to dedicated, 2) maintain existing requests for 2 minutes (drain), 3) re-route to hosted, 4) keep dedicated live for postmortem snapshot for 1 hour.

Stress schedule suggestions (to pick exact windows with Peregrine):
- Dry-run mirror: Sep 28 02:00–06:00 UTC (low customer impact window)
- Production blackout for swap: Oct 12 00:00–04:00 UTC (target)

I will produce the automation runbook and the CLI commands we will execute for the switch and the rollback.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Draft acceptance checklist and switchback windows below — please review and flag any missing items. This is what procurement will sign off on as the acceptance criteria.

Pre-swap acceptance (required):
- Mirrored run completed with three passes and p99 <= 350ms on at least 2/3 passes.
- No 5xx spikes > 0.5% during mirrors.
- KV cache hit >= 20% during steady-state pass.
- Observability: dashboards populated, alert rules and traces ingesting, and on-call paging configured.
- Security: VPC peering confirmed and access list for staging tokens rotated.

Cutover timeline (proposed):
- Sep 28: Dry-run mirror (validation).
- Oct 5: Internal preflight (internal traffic only, light ingress).
- Oct 12: Production swap (00:00–04:00 UTC) with a 90-minute guarded-monitor window.

Switchback (if triggered):
- Trigger: any FAIL threshold per Karthik's list.
- Maximum decision window: 30 minutes after alert (team to decide).
- Rollback execution time target: < 20 minutes from decision to full traffic back on hosted.

Post-swap acceptance:
- 24-hour burn-in with daily check-ins.
- Cost reconciliation report (first 3 days).

Procurement asked for: a signed SOW addendum with the rollback/acceptance clauses and a DocuSign link. I can draft the addendum if you want — Markus?

-Neha
Director, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
